introduction: ERC-5269 defines an interface for detecting which ERCs a smart contract supports, identifying each standard by its ERC number, not a hashed function selector. It was proposed by Zainan Victor Zhou in July 2022. Its core method, supportERC, takes a caller, an ERC number, and a sub-behavior identifier, and returns a bytes32 status such as keccak256("FINAL"). Contracts may also emit an OnSupportERC event to advertise support. Note: ERC-5269 is in Review status; the interface may still change before it is finalized.
designPurpose: ERC-5269 was designed to address limitations of ERC-165. ERC-165 hashes a method signature, so it cannot describe standards that define no method, such as data-format or signature schemes, and it cannot answer differently depending on who is asking. ERC-5269 instead queries support by ERC number, which is human-readable and easier to use with named contracts such as ENS, and it adds a caller parameter so a contract can report different support for different callers, as with a transparent proxy admin.
commonUsage: Because ERC-5269 competes with the widely used ERC-165, it is intended for contracts that want to advertise the ERCs they implement in a human-readable form. A contract emits OnSupportERC(address(0), 5269, 0, status) on construction or upgrade to declare its compliance, and callers can query supportERC to learn whether a given standard is available to an address. The specification illustrates the pattern with an ERC-721 contract that also declares support for its Metadata and Enumerable extensions.
fn.supportERC.desc: Returns a bytes32 status indicating whether the contract supports the ERC given by majorERCIdentifier and the sub-behavior in minorERCIdentifier. Returns keccak256("FINAL") for Final ERCs; a zero return means not supported.
fn.supportERC.params.caller: The address whose access to the queried ERC is being checked; support may vary by caller.
fn.supportERC.params.majorERCIdentifier: The ERC number being queried, which should be in the range (0, 2^32-1].
fn.supportERC.params.minorERCIdentifier: A bytes32 identifier for a sub-behavior; a value of 0 refers to the main behavior of the ERC.
fn.supportERC.params.extraData: Extra calldata reserved for ERC-5750 style future extensions.
fn.supportERC.returns.ercStatus: A bytes32 status: keccak256("FINAL") for Final ERCs, keccak256("DRAFT") or another documented value otherwise, and 0 for unsupported.
fn.OnSupportERC.desc: Optionally emitted, typically on construction or upgrade, to declare that the contract supports a given ERC or sub-behavior. An emission with caller address(0) applies to all callers.
fn.OnSupportERC.params.caller: The caller the declaration applies to; address(0) means all callers.
fn.OnSupportERC.params.majorERCIdentifie: The ERC number the contract is declaring support for.
fn.OnSupportERC.params.minorERCIdentifie: The sub-behavior identifier; a value of 0 means the entire ERC.
fn.OnSupportERC.params.ercStatus: The status value declared for the ERC, such as keccak256("FINAL").
fn.OnSupportERC.params.extraData: Additional data reserved for future extensions.
sim.supportQueryWalkthrough.name: Support Query Walkthrough
sim.supportQueryWalkthrough.desc: Query a contract for whether it supports a given ERC number using supportERC(), then see how the contract advertises support.
sim.supportQueryWalkthrough.step.call: The caller invokes supportERC(caller, majorERCIdentifier, minorERCIdentifier, extraData) on the contract to ask whether an ERC is supported.
sim.supportQueryWalkthrough.step.lookup: The view function checks the contract's declared support for the requested ERC number and sub-behavior, without mutating any state.
sim.supportQueryWalkthrough.step.return: The contract returns the bytes32 status, such as keccak256("DRAFTv1") here; a zero value would mean the ERC is not supported.
sim.supportQueryWalkthrough.step.declare: Separately, the contract emits OnSupportERC on construction or upgrade so indexers can discover the ERCs it supports.
